full_judgment:
3. Defendant Nos.1 and 2 contested the suit by filing joint written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. They contended, inter alia, that the survey was done collusively and the khatian was prepared in the name of Abdul Hashem with others, which was not proper and as such, the same is liable to corrected. The defendants also filed additional statement on 07.03.2010, contending, inter alia, that the plaintiff has no right title in the suit property and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. Mr. Md. Helal Amin, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division committed a patent error, inasmuch as the suit was filed for permanent injunction and as such it is an important element to ascertain as to who is in possession of the suit land. But the trial Court without discussing all evidence on record decided the possession of the plaintiff and decreed the suit. The High Court Division also without going through the depositions of P.Ws. and evidence on record came to an erroneous finding and decision and thus made the Rule absolute. He further submitted that the High Court Division committed an error making the Rule absolute, inasmuch as it ought not to have considered materials beyond the record, as such it is liable to be examined by this Division. The trial Court without elaborate discussion of documentary and oral evidence and only on the basis of B.R.S. Khatian and the purchase deed exhibited by the plaintiff decreed the suit by an unprecedented short judgment. He also submitted that the appellate Court went through the evidence and materials on record, and discussed the all P.Ws. and D.Ws. elaborately and came to a proper decision and reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The High Court Division in the absence of the learned Advocate for the opposite party-petitioner herein, and without going through the evidence on record; considering only the submissions of the learned Advocate of the plaintiff and the judgment of trial Court made the Rule absolute. He submitted that the High Court Division committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in not considering that a civil Court has ample jurisdiction to examine the evidence on record and to examine whether any laws and rules have been properly applied. But the trial Court without going through the same decreed the suit and decided the possession in favour of the plaintiff as such the judgment and order of the High Court Division upholding the decree of the trial Court calls for interference by this Division. He submitted that the trial Court as well as High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering that the plaintiff stated in Para-3 of his plaint that he is owning and possessing the suit land with full knowledge of the defendants and others, but the same was not supported by P.W.2 Abdul Gofur. He deposed that Abdul Mannan (plaintiff) has been possessing the suit land for about 2 years and prior to that the possession of the suit land was with Fazu Kha, A. Goni Kha for long 40 years and thereafter by one Hashem Master. P.W.2 also in cross examination stated the same. P.W.3 Hasen Miah deposed that the plaintiff Abdul Mannan took crops in the last harvest and the one before that. In cross examination P.W.3 stated that Rumali Kha, Buju Kha and Goni Kha did not take the crops in his presence, and that he had seen them cultivating the suit land for about 40 years. P.W.1-plaintiff in cross examination stated that Hashem took over the land by Kabuliyat but the so-called Kabuliyat was not produced before the trial Court as exhibit. The High Court Division without controverting the aforesaid aspect and evidence made the Rule absolute. He lastly submitted that the trial Court and the High Court Division also committed an error of law misreading and finding the exhibits of defendants, but the appellate Court filled up the said lacuna of trial Court and came to proper finding and decision. Hence the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.
